name: MC33174DTBR2G
title: MC33171, MC33172, MC33174 and NCV33172, NCV33174: single, dual and quad low-power bipolar op amps, 3.0 V to 44 V supply
summary: A family of bipolar operational amplifiers that draw about 180 µA per amplifier and give 1.8 MHz gain-bandwidth and 2.1 V/µs slew rate. They run from a single 3.0 V to 44 V supply or from ±1.5 V to ±22 V, and the input common-mode range reaches down to the negative rail, so single-supply circuits can take signals at ground. The output stage is built only from NPN transistors, with no crossover deadband, and drives up to 500 pF. MC33171 is the single (with offset-null pins), MC33172 the dual and MC33174 the quad; MC33174DTBR2G is the quad in TSSOP-14 for −40 °C to +85 °C.
key_figures: 3.0 V to 44 V single, ±1.5 V to ±22 V split
180 µA typ, 250 µA max per amplifier (VCC = 5.0 V, 25 °C)

circuits.title: AC coupled non-inverting amplifier on a single +5.0 V supply
circuits.description: Gain of 101 with a −3 dB bandwidth of 20 kHz. A 510 kΩ / 2.2 kΩ divider from VCC holds a node about 21 mV above ground, and 100 kΩ carries that bias to the non-inverting input, so the input sits just inside the common-mode range at the negative rail. The signal arrives through Cin. The 1.0 kΩ to ground and the 100 kΩ from the output set the gain at DC too, which lifts the output to roughly 2.2 V and leaves room for a 3.6 Vpp swing. CO blocks the DC level from the 100 kΩ load.
notes: AV = 101; BW (−3.0 dB) = 20 kHz; output 3.6 Vpp.

circuits.title: AC coupled inverting amplifier on a single +5.0 V supply
circuits.description: Gain of −10 with a −3 dB bandwidth of 200 kHz. Two 100 kΩ resistors split VCC to bias the non-inverting input at mid-supply, with a capacitor from that node to ground. The signal comes in through Cin and a 10 kΩ resistor to the inverting input and a 10 kΩ feedback resistor closes the loop, so the DC gain is one and the output rests at the bias. CO couples the 3.8 Vpp output to the 100 kΩ load.
notes: AV = 10; BW (−3.0 dB) = 200 kHz; output 3.8 Vpp.

circuits.title: DC coupled inverting amplifier, maximum output swing on a single +5.0 V supply
circuits.description: Gain of −10 with a −3 dB bandwidth of 200 kHz and a 4.2 Vpp output centred on 2.5 V. The load, 50 kΩ, returns to VCC rather than ground, so it pulls the output up on positive swings and the output stage only has to sink. A 100 kΩ / 4.7 kΩ divider with a filter capacitor sets the non-inverting input near 0.22 V; the source drives the inverting input through 100 kΩ and 1.0 MΩ is the feedback.
notes: AV = 10; BW (−3.0 dB) = 200 kHz; VO = 2.5 V with 4.2 Vpp swing.

circuits.title: Offset nulling (MC33171)
circuits.description: Trim of the input offset on the single MC33171. A 10 kΩ potentiometer spans the two offset-null pins, 1 and 5, and its wiper goes to VEE. The trim range is about ±80 mV. The dual and quad have no null pins.

parts.note: potentiometer; pins 1 and 2 are the track ends, W the wiper

circuits.title: Active high-Q notch filter, 1.0 kHz
circuits.description: A twin-T network ahead of a unity-gain follower. One branch is two 16 kΩ resistors in series with 0.01 µF from their junction; the other is two 0.02 µF capacitors in series with 32 kΩ from their junction. Both shunt legs return to the follower output instead of to ground, which bootstraps the network and sharpens the notch. The input must sit at 0.2 V DC or more.
notes: fo = 1.0 kHz; fo = 1 / (4πRC).

circuits.title: Active bandpass filter, 30 kHz, Q = 10
circuits.description: A multiple-feedback bandpass with centre frequency 30 kHz, Q of 10 and unity gain at the centre. The input reaches a node through R1, 1.1 kΩ; R2, 5.6 kΩ, goes from that node to ground. One 0.047 µF capacitor runs from the node to the output and another from the node to the inverting input, and R3, 2.2 kΩ, is the feedback from output to inverting input. The non-inverting input is held at 0.4 VCC.

operation.text: MC33171 holds one amplifier, MC33172 two and MC33174 four. Parts with V in the name and the NCV parts cover −40 °C to +125 °C; the others −40 °C to +85 °C. The NCV versions are AEC-Q100 qualified and PPAP capable for automotive use. Packages: PDIP-8 and SO-8 for the single and dual, PDIP-14, SO-14 and TSSOP-14 for the quad. The parts are Pb-free, halogen free and RoHS compliant.

Each amplifier has a PNP Darlington differential input and an output stage made only of NPN transistors. There is no JFET in the design. The input capacitance is 0.8 pF, against about 3.0 pF for a typical JFET input, which helps frequency response with high source resistance. The NPN output has no crossover deadband, its gain and phase change little between sourcing and sinking, and it is faster than a PNP stage.

The input common-mode range includes VEE, so the amplifier works from a single supply down to 3.0 V with the inputs at ground. The single-supply figures are given at 5.0 V; the parts still work at 3.0 V at 25 °C, with small shifts in DC gain, slew rate and bandwidth.

operation.topic: Input voltage limits and phase reversal
operation.text: Differential input voltage may reach 44 V as long as both inputs stay between VCC and VEE. Without damage, though not recommended, an input can go about 3.0 V above VCC or 0.3 V below VEE, and up to 5.0 mA can be drawn out of VEE through an input clamp diode without latch-up; in either case the output may reverse phase. There is no reversal while one input is inside the common-mode range and the other inside the maximum input range. With both inputs above the upper common-mode limit the output goes to its lowest level. The dual and quad have ESD protection diodes on the inputs.

A feedback resistor and the input capacitance form a pole that makes the loop second order and slows settling, as in current-to-voltage conversion after a DAC. A small capacitor across the feedback resistor adds a zero that cancels it and cuts overshoot. With 10 kΩ feedback and a 10 V step, settling takes typically 4.2 µs to ½ LSB of 8 bits and 4.8 µs to ½ LSB of 12 bits.

As an inverting unity-gain stage the slew rate is about ±2.1 V/µs, the same both ways. As a non-inverting follower the rising slew is also 2.1 V/µs and the falling slew is usually faster, depending on how fast the input falls.

Into 10 kΩ the output typically comes within 0.8 V of either rail: 28.4 Vpp on ±15 V, an advantage that shows most at low supply. The top of the swing is set by the saturation of current source Q7, the VBE of pull-up Q17 and the drop across short-circuit resistor R5. Below 0.4 mA of sink current the bottom is set by the saturation of pull-down Q15 and the drops on R4 and R5, so a light load lets the output come within millivolts of VEE. Above 0.4 mA, diode D3 clamps R4 and the low limit becomes about VEE + 1.0 V.

On a single supply the widest swing comes with the load tied to VCC instead of ground: the load pulls the output up and the amplifier pulls it down near ground. The load resistance should be much smaller than the feedback resistance.

Without a PNP emitter follower at the output, the amplifier sinks at least 15 mA, typically down to an output of VEE + 1.8 V. On a single supply the output can source or sink the base current of a common-emitter NPN transistor directly for switching.

Open-loop output impedance at 1.0 MHz is low, 100 Ω to 200 Ω typical, and a non-inverting unity-gain stage drives 0 pF to 400 pF without oscillating; capacitive drive of 0 pF to 500 pF is also quoted. Phase margin is 60° and gain margin 15 dB, and both barely change with the output swing, so compensation does not have to allow for it. The parts suit active filters, especially on a low single supply.
Supply applied backwards, or the chip put in a socket the wrong way round, drives large currents through it with nothing to limit them and can destroy it.

Long unshielded leads at the input or output couple the two. Resistors that connect to an input should sit right at the pin, keeping stray capacitance off the input node, which helps frequency response and cuts pick-up. Decouple the supply with enough capacitance right at the supply pin, keeping in mind that many capacitor types change impedance a great deal with temperature.

Every output is current limited and survives a short to ground, but the junction must stay within its maximum temperature. On ±15 V supplies one output can usually stay shorted to ground indefinitely without going past that limit.
Only the single MC33171 has offset-null pins (1 and 5). A 10 kΩ potentiometer across them with its wiper at VEE trims about ±80 mV.
